headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and secrets while botpress lacks isolation and may ingest shared outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write workspace files and use MCP/browser/web channels, so if botpress outputs are placed in a shared workspace or webhook path, prompt-like content could be re-ingested. botpress itself has no documented isolation or provenance controls, so the pair has a plausible injection bridge in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF botpress outputs are written into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or another shared file path, injection becomes reachable.
IF nullclaw consumes MCP/webhook content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer it.
mitigations: Separate botpress and nullclaw into distinct workspaces.
Disable MCP/webhook ingestion for untrusted botpress outputs.
Add a manual review step before nullclaw acts on botpress-generated text.
Use read-only handoff files for botpress outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, and it has broad network egress. botpress has no documented filesystem isolation or secret-handling controls. If they share a workspace or botpress forwards content into nullclaw, sensitive data can be exposed or exfiltrated by default behavior.
conditions: IF botpress and nullclaw share ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or another writable directory, leakage is reachable.
IF botpress content includes secrets or customer data and nullclaw processes it, those data enter a broad-egress agent.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace directories.
Mount botpress and nullclaw on separate volumes.
Rotate any secrets already present in shared files.
Restrict nullclaw network egress during testing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret redaction and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; botpress can install packages. In a shared repo or workspace, both agents can mutate the same state without any documented locking or coordination, creating direct write conflicts and nondeterministic corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or workspace directory, write conflicts are reachable.
IF botpress installs packages while nullclaw modifies files in the same environment, state drift can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Freeze package installation during concurrent runs.
Serialize git writes through one operator.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, and shell/browser tools, so if it treats botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. botpress is a customer-support agent and may generate conversational content that nullclaw then operationalizes without verification, which is a classic unsafe handoff.
conditions: IF botpress output is fed directly into nullclaw's stdin/stdout, webhook, or file inputs, the cascade is reachable.
IF nullclaw executes shell or API actions based on unverified botpress text, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Require human approval before nullclaw acts on botpress output.
Add schema validation for botpress-to-nullclaw handoffs.
Log and diff botpress outputs before execution.
Disable automatic action-taking on first-pass responses.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates and typed contracts.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles audit logs, workspace files, and multiple secret classes, while botpress is a customer-support agent that may process customer data. The profiles do not document residency or retention alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible even though no specific jurisdictional breach is proven.
conditions: IF customer-support data from botpress is stored in nullclaw audit logs or workspace files, retention scope expands.
IF either deployment has stricter residency or deletion requirements than the other, mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Review retention settings for both agents.
Exclude regulated data from shared logs.
Document data-flow boundaries.
Purge stale workspace files before joint runs.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion policies across both systems.
